audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers gave Cho'Gath all seven rows while whys[0], whys[1], whys[2] and whys[4] all say the row is even, and the packet chart has Skill on those four rows.
audit.why: Pre-Feast this is a poke lane a 950-range marker wins; Cho'Gath's edge is levels 4-5, first item and 2+ items, where Feast stacks push his health past the execute threshold. The mirror audit settled on exactly this chart.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 1, 2 and 4 flipped to Skill in BOTH layers, ratings rebuilt to 5/5/5/3/5/4/3 from Locke's side. HARD 7/10 overall kept — 47.39% over 555 games.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags zero cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere in this matchup, and Feast was described without a range or a cooldown.
audit.why: Feast is 175 range on 80/70/60s — he has to be in melee range to cast it, and missing it costs him over a minute. Rupture is 6s flat, Feral Scream 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s. Those numbers are the whole 'when not to fight' answer.
audit.corrected: 175 range and 80s stated in spikes[1] and late; 6s Rupture in early; the 11s Feral Scream in mid and spikes[3].

audit.whatIsWrong: Locke's Q was called Ritual Nails and his passive Silver Stake; Cho'Gath's silence was written as part of Rupture ('Q Rupture + Silence') rather than as Feral Scream.
audit.why: Riot's text: Rupture pops enemies into the air, damages and slows — no silence. Feral Scream is the silence, a 300-range cone. The silence is the ability that strands Locke's E, so attributing it to the wrong button makes the advice untrackable. Locke's Q is Soul Nails and his passive is unnamed in the file.
audit.corrected: Feral Scream named as the silence with its cooldown; Rupture described as knockup and slow; Soul Nails used; passive described by its missing-health on-hit effect.

audit.why: Rupture carries a derived grounding flag that Riot's description does not support — knockup and slow only — so no grounding claim was written on his side.

edits.before: Your Q Ritual Nails poke wins the early trade window before Cho'Gath's Vorpal Spikes and Feast stacks give him permanent bulk, so shove and chip while he's small.
edits.after: Your Q Soul Nails poke wins the early trade window before Cho'Gath's Vorpal Spikes and Feast stacks give him permanent bulk, so shove and chip while he is still small.

edits.before: Cho'Gath hits 6 and gains Feast — a point-and-click true-damage execute that also permanently grows his HP, which directly counters your R Purgatory threshold math by inflating the health pool you're trying to execute.
edits.after: Cho'Gath hits 6 and gains Feast — a 175-range true-damage devour on an 80s cooldown that permanently grows his HP whenever it kills, inflating the very health pool your R Purgatory threshold has to reach.

edits.before: Full-stack Feast Cho'Gath is a raid boss your execute totem can't reach — his HP is far above your R's growing threshold and his Q Rupture + Silence chains your engage into death.
edits.after: Full-stack Feast Cho'Gath is a raid boss your execute cannot reach — his HP sits far above your R's threshold, and Rupture into an 11s Feral Scream silence strands your E and kills you.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are even skill — your P Silver Stake missing-HP procs and Q Ritual Nails poke actually chip Cho'Gath faster than his short-range Vorpal Spikes can answer, so freeze near your side and punish his last-hits. Avoid standing in the center of a caster wave where his Q Rupture can catch you.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are even skill — your missing-HP on-hit procs and Q Soul Nails poke chip Cho'Gath faster than his 40-range Vorpal Spikes can answer, so freeze near your side and punish his last-hits. Avoid the centre of a caster wave, where his 6s Q Rupture catches you for free.

edits.before: By Levels 4-5 Cho'Gath tips ahead: Feast at 6 gives him a true-damage point-click execute plus permanent HP growth that neutralizes your R Purgatory math. Your W Soul Ignition self-damage is dangerous here because his Q Rupture + Silence can lock your E Ashen Pursuit escape and turn your grey-health into a real deficit. Only commit if you can burst him below Feast-execute range first.
edits.after: By Levels 4-5 Cho'Gath tips ahead: Feast at 6 is true damage plus permanent HP growth that neutralises your R Purgatory math. Your W Soul Ignition self-damage is dangerous here because Rupture into Feral Scream's silence strands your E Ashen Pursuit escape and turns grey health into a real deficit. Commit only when he has spent one of those two.

edits.before: With items and Feast stacks Cho'Gath is a wall — his HP climbs far above your R's growing threshold so your execute totem simply won't trigger, and one Q Rupture into Feast deletes you. Don't force top; use your E mobility to roam and let your team peel him.
edits.after: With items and Feast stacks Cho'Gath is a wall — his HP climbs far above your R's threshold so the execute never triggers, and one Rupture into a 175-range Feast deletes you. Don't force top; use your E to roam and let your team peel him.

edits.before: Trade with Q Ritual Nails marks before he stacks Feast
edits.after: Trade with Q Soul Nails marks before he stacks Feast

notes: Feast has 175 range — he must be effectively in melee to cast it, which is the single most actionable fact in the lane and appeared nowhere. The full layer tracks 'Rupture (Knockup)' as the focus ability in a dozen fields; the name is right, the parenthetical is cosmetic, so I left it. Ratings on rows 3, 5 and 6 (3/10, 4/10, 3/10) already read correctly from Locke's side and were left as-is, so only the four flipped rows changed rating.
